text:
nik: quick follow-up on the dedicated-gpu autoscale RFC. im worried the current SLA-weight idea is too binary: either you get burst tokens or you dont. propose a small evolution: SLO-ladder + credit envelopes. tenants get a ladder of SLO bands (e.g. gold/silver/bronze) with separate credit envelopes that replenish based on observed latency and cost signals. when a band is exhausted we pick the least disruptive degrade path configured by tenant.

maria: interesting. so lane = {slo_target, credit_capacity, refill_policy}? that lets us express e.g. gold=100 qps @ p95<200ms, silver=200 qps @ p95<400ms, etc.

sam: makes sense. refill_policy could be time-based or signal-based (p95-driven). prefer signal-driven refill: if backpressure lowers p95 we can restore credits faster.

lee: tradeoffs: complexity vs UX. also, where does the evaluator live? my vote: a control-plane microservice that subscribes to telemetry and exposes an admission HTTP endpoint. runtime asks the proxy for admission decisions, proxy returns allow/reject/fallback and optional headers.

nik: proxy approach ok. we must avoid added tail latency: cache positive decisions for a short TTL in the runtime (e.g. 200ms) to avoid roundtrip on hot paths. also allow offline dry-run mode for policy tuning.

maria: policy sketch (human readable):
```
bands:
  - name: gold
    slo_p95_ms: 200
    credit_capacity: 1200
    refill: 
      type: signal
      signal: p95
      params: {ewma_window_s:60, min_refill_per_min:50}
  - name: silver
    slo_p95_ms: 400
    credit_capacity: 2400
fallbacks:
  on_deplete: [reject_with_retry, fallback_variant]
```

sam: important: make decisions pure and deterministic. dry-run must produce identical decisions to enforced mode. we should version policies and include a policy_id in audit records.

lee: ops signals required: emit `credit_envelope_depleted` and `band_reinstated` events with tenant_id, band, action, and decision_reason. also emit estimated time-to-depletion forecast as a gauge.

infra-bot: canary deploy: autoscaler-proxy v1.0 canary in cluster-c. no failures reported.

nik: good. another question: fallback semantics. in-order variant fallback is ok, but some tenants want concurrent mix (e.g. route 20% to cheaper model when silver depleted). suggest policy supports weights per fallback.

maria: +1 for weighted fallback. add a simple sampling mechanism in runtime that honors weights to keep deterministic behavior per-request-id.

sam: also consider client-facing error shape when rejecting: 429 with machine_code `SLA_BAND_EXHAUSTED`, Retry-After seconds, and a `X-Redwood-Console-URL` header linking to opt-in toggles. SDKs can detect the code and implement exponential jittered backoff.

lee: testing: build a sim harness that replays historical traces and runs the evaluator to produce per-tenant CSV with columns: tenant_id, band_hits, band_depletes, fallbacks_used, rejections, est_cost_delta, p95_delta. the harness should support variable policy versions.

maria: i can own the sim harness. plan: 1 day trace, 5 minute windows, EWMA smoothing. will output CSV and a simple viz of top-10 affected tenants.

sam: ill design the proxy API proto: /admit -> {tenant, route, tokens, model, request_id} -> {decision, action, headers, policy_id, reason}. keep payload small.

nik: rollout plan: (1) implement pure evaluator + sim, (2) deploy proxy in dry-run for 1 week with audit stream only, (3) enable enforcement for a pilot set (3 tenants), (4) add weighted fallbacks and expand.

lee: metrics shape: counters for decisions (allow/reject/fallback), histogram for decision_latency, gauge for credit_balance per tenant-band, and forecast_ttd gauge. tag with tenant_id and policy_id.

audit-bot: note: kafka topic `sla-policy-decisions.v1` ready. retention=14d.

nik: logging/telemetry: decisions written as ndjson to kafka topic with fields: timestamp, policy_id, tenant_id, decision, reason, request_id, latency_ms. keep payload small. also sample 1% of full request traces and link to decision id for debugging.

maria: who owns the policy UI in Console? product needs to show band definitions, current credit balance, and quick opt-in toggle for fallbacks. ticket created: WEB-876.

sam: one more corner: preemptible eviction. when cloud preemptions spike, we may want to temporarily raise refill rates to avoid mass rejects. proxy should accept a cluster_health signal to bias refill upward during evacuation.

lee: agree. cluster_health signal can be a simple boolean with severity. keep logic conservative.

nik: ok follow-ups: maria -> sim PR, sam -> proxy proto PR, lee -> metrics + error format PR, sam+nik -> policy schema PR. post PR links here. thanks all :tada:
